Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

School & learning

calculator noun

also pocket calculator, calculating machine

modern

Traupman 28

māchinula calculātōria

a calculator

A little machine for reckoning, built from late words on classical stems: māchinula is in Paulinus of Nola, calculātōrius, of an accountant, in a scholiast on Juvenal (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Digitīs computā, nōn māchinulā!

    Work it out on your fingers, not with the calculator!composed

Other words

  • māchina arithmētica — a calculating machine

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. calculator, after Leibniz

    Leibniz’s name for his calculating machine; Morgan–Owens also gives Egger’s mēchanēma calculātōrium.

  • calculātor, calculātōris m. — a teacher of arithmetic; an accountant

    noun, third declension · avoid · classical · Mart. 10.62.4 (Lewis & Short)

    A false friend: in Martial the arithmetic master, beside the shorthand master, and in the Digest a bookkeeper; not a machine.

See also sum, arithmetic, maths, computer.

SourcesLewis & Short: machinula · Lewis & Short: calculatorius · Lewis & Short: machina · Lewis & Short: calculator

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. calculator.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 28, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
